title: Jazz albums in Los Angeles: Shorty Rogers, JATP, Cy Touff
summary: Edison lists albums made in Los Angeles, including at the Hague club and Cy Touff's date.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: sometimes I would do three in one day, you know. And after I -- oh, it was just so many artists around here I used to record with. And I did a lot of work with Shorty Rogers, you know. Did an album with him. Did albums with JATP for Norman , Ben Webster. Jimmy Rowles, Joe Mondragon, then I made an album here at the Hague, that nightclub across from the Ambassador Hotel, with Arnold Ross.
Oh, I remember that. That made quite a bit of noise, that album, in New York, as I remember.
Yes, it did. Joe Comfort, I think, was on bass. And -- oh, I forget the drummer's name.
Well, I could look that up, couldn't I.
Yeah. That was made for Pacific, though.
You were going to New York now and forming your quintet.
Yeah, my quintet. I was trying to think of who was in the band at the Hague. That was a good album.

Then I made another album out here called -- one tune was on there called "Keyster Parade". It was Conrad Gozzo Richard Kamuca , Chuck Flores on drums and oh, it was a fantastic date. The bass trumpet player in Chicago, he wrote all the arrangements.
Well, was this in your name or --
No, that was under Cy Touff's name. And that was for Pacific Jazz, you know. And I did so much recording out here, with Shorty Rogers, as I said, and just everybody.
